synopsis: Komatsu KomVision is a human-detection and collision-mitigation product for hydraulic excavators, used in the booklet as a market precedent rather than a simulation tool; it launched on the PC200-11 in Japan in December 2019, followed by the PC200i-12 in December 2024 [f16089, f1641, f1640]. It detects people using cameras and machine learning, while radar on the -12 supports detection of people and objects; false and missed detections depend on weather and surrounding conditions [f1644, f1645]. Its emergency stop operates via the lock lever at travel or swing start, not during an ongoing swing, and the skeptic's review describes operation only at slow travel speeds or motion start [f1642, f11426, f10439]. The travel condition is described as “Low-speed travel,” but numerical speeds and detection ranges were not found, leaving its quantified operating envelope unclear [f1643]. KomVision must be switched off during trailer loading because a rapid stop can destabilize the machine, and Komatsu offered a software update to retrofit existing KomVision machines [f1646, f11427, f10983].
